experience.player_does: Launch the game, press Play, and read a hand-authored cell map containing a roof, a directional arrow, and a water edge. Each catalogued shape can turn in quarter steps, and each cell's shape colour sits on its own palette-coloured background.
experience.feels_like: The map reads like a small visual alphabet rather than a tile texture: a few repeated squares and triangles are enough to sketch recognisable things, while contrasting foreground and background colours make each mark legible. Adding a future primitive should mean adding geometry to the catalog, not adding another renderer branch.
experience.camera: Keep the fixed 1920×1080 logical view and existing top-left map presentation; this slice changes cell grammar and drawing, not camera behaviour.
experience.controls: No new controls. Existing Play and Quit behaviour remains unchanged.
experience.not_this: Not free-form drawing, not layered shapes inside one cell, and not a map editor; the probe uses only two catalog entries even though the renderer is ready to consume more.

design_refs.why: The settled cell grammar requires one shape per cell, quarter-turn draw-time rotation, and two palette indices so recognizable compositions can be built from a small vocabulary.
The map probe must remain plain, versioned, strict, data-only text that a future runtime editor can read and write without ambiguity.

considered_existing.why_not: It already owns row-token parsing and packed cell access, so it is the correct owner to extend rather than creating a second cell or token module.
It already owns version checks, strict schema validation, and the external JSON boundary; the format version and layer parsing belong here.
It already owns map presentation and is the right thin node layer for drawing triangles and applying cell rotations; a renderer module would split a currently single-purpose view prematurely.
The existing authored map is the end-to-end visual probe surface; replacing its rows with the slice-2 examples exercises the real loader instead of adding a disconnected fixture.
The existing map-format tests already cover the single validator and round-trip boundary, so the new grammar and compatibility cases belong beside them.

modules.role: Own the strict versioned map document, the scalable shape catalog, and conversion of v1/v2 row tokens into typed packed cell values containing shape, rotation, foreground, and background indices.
modules.why: Rotation and a second colour change the persisted cell contract, while a catalog keeps primitive geometry out of the renderer; keeping both in the existing data module prevents Variant-backed map values from reaching presentation code.
modules.boundary_data: External JSON enters as Variant-backed Dictionary/Array values and leaves as LevelFormat, LevelLayer, PackedColorArray, PackedStringArray, and packed integer cell values.

modules.role: Render the typed cell values into the existing logical canvas, drawing the cell background first and any catalogued polygon foreground second.
modules.why: The slice must answer the visual hand-authoring question end to end; the existing presentation owner can use one generic polygon path so future primitives do not multiply renderer branches.
modules.boundary_data: Receives typed LevelLayer values and palette colours, then emits CanvasItem draw calls only.

modules.role: Exercise the versioned cell grammar and map round-trip without instantiating the presentation scene.
modules.why: The parser and packed representation need deterministic coverage for two colours, four rotations, triangles, strict invalid tokens, and legacy v1 maps.
modules.boundary_data: Constructs typed LevelFormat values from test dictionaries and observes validation, accessors, and serialization results.

files.why: Extend row tokens from legacy shape-plus-colour to v2 shape-id-plus-foreground-plus-background-plus-rotation, while retaining explicit typed accessors and v1 loading.
Describe normalized polygon geometry and stable two-character shape ids in one typed catalog so adding primitives does not require a new draw function.
Advance the authored map format to version 2, accept version 1 for compatibility, and pass the document version into the single layer validator.
Draw every cell background from its background palette index, then render any catalogued polygon with the cell's quarter-turn rotation.
Prove v2 parsing, two-colour round trips, all quarter-turn values, catalogued triangle recognition, strict rejection, and v1 compatibility.
Verify the shape catalog exposes stable ids and polygon geometry independently from the scene renderer.
Hand-author the roof, arrow, and water-edge probe that makes the new vocabulary visible in the running game.

revisions.what: Replaced the triangle-specific renderer function and four-character token with a generic polygon draw path backed by a two-character shape-id catalog.
revisions.why: Human review identified that a special function would scale poorly as the primitive vocabulary grows toward dozens of shapes.

revisions.what: The catalog initializes its typed polygon arrays in an instance and the generic renderer calls it through one catalog instance; the rotation parameter is named quarter_turns.
revisions.why: Godot 4.7.1 rejects PackedVector2Array literals as constant expressions and Control already owns a rotation property, so the original static geometry and rotation parameter would not type-check.

functions.why: Parse each layer with the document version so legacy two-character tokens and v2 five-character tokens with scalable shape ids have explicit compatibility rules.

functions.why: Validate the correct token grammar and palette references before any layer becomes drawable.

functions.why: Keep the four typed cell attributes in one compact value at the data/presentation boundary.
Expose the shape without duplicating bit layout knowledge in the node layer.

Expose the shape colour index to the renderer.
Expose the independent cell background colour index to the renderer.
